approachQuestion.prompt:
Detect a nearby repeated signal

Input: an integer array signals and a nonnegative integer k. Return true exactly when there exist indices i<j with signals[i]=signals[j] and j−i≤k. Return false otherwise.

Example 1: signals = [4,8,4], k = 2. Output: true. Example 2: signals = [4,8,4], k = 1. Output: false. Example 3: signals = [7,7], k = 0. Output: false. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000 and 0 ≤ k ≤ 200,000.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Return false immediately for k=0. Otherwise scan with a set of the last at most k values: before testing index j, remove signals[j−k−1] if that index exists; return true on membership, else insert signals[j].
options.feedback: Before each query the set represents exactly the eligible prior indices. If an equal value had already existed within that retained interval, the scan would already have returned true, so removal by value is safe.

options.text: Store every value’s latest index without deleting old keys. On a repeat, compare the distance to k and return true if it qualifies.
options.feedback: This is correct for the whole domain, but retains values from arbitrarily distant history. Expiring old entries bounds working storage by the permitted distance.

options.text: Build a set of all signal values; return true if its size is smaller than the input length and k is positive.
options.feedback: [4,8,4] with k=1 contains a repeat but its only pair is too far apart.

options.text: For k>0, insert the current value into a set of recent values, then test whether that value is present.
options.feedback: The test always finds the just-inserted value. signals [7] with k=1 must return false, since no distinct prior position exists.

feedback.reason: Expire irrelevant history before a membership query so retained state matches a distance-bounded eligibility rule.
details: If k=0 return false. Otherwise maintain a set. At each index j, first remove the value at j−k−1 when this index exists, then test the current value; return true if present, otherwise insert it. Return false after the scan. Stop at the first successful query, so retained values are distinct until termination.

Expire indices older than j-k before querying. Until the first match, retained values are distinct, making removal by value safe. Inserting before querying would falsely match the current index to itself.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Detect a nearby repeated signal — analyzed method”, n is array length; state the worst-input bound by n with k allowed to vary as an input parameter. For k=0 the method returns in constant time. Deleted set entries release logical storage and capacity is bounded by peak live entries. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.
constraints: Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + 1) worst-input time; O(min(n,k) + 1) auxiliary space.
Expected O(n + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space even when k is bounded, as the tight bound.
Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space for all k.

feedback.reason: Maintain only distance-eligible keys with expected constant work per index.
details: Expire irrelevant history before a membership query so retained state matches a distance-bounded eligibility rule.
For k>0, each index performs at most one deletion, one lookup and one insertion, so expected O(n+1) worst-input time. k=0 returns immediately; some repeated-signal inputs also terminate early.

Before a query there are at most k prior values; insertion can briefly retain k+1 distinct values. Thus O(min(n,k)+1), including empty input, k=0 and constant scalar/stack state. No stale-history map is retained.
“Expected O(n + 1) worst-input time; O(min(n,k) + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.

“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space even when k is bounded, as the tight bound.”: Expiration limits the retained keys to at most k+1 while processing, so O(n) loses the tighter distance-dependent bound.
“Expected O(nk + 1) time; O(min(n,k) + 1) space.”: The method queries membership rather than scanning all k prior positions.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space for all k.”: When k grows with n, the set may retain a growing number of distinct eligible values.
